Overview › Allergen

Allergen

The allergen wall — a positive-evidence exclusion that runs on every recipe surface: an always-on SQL WHERE on all browse/list paths (excluded on self-report or ingredient-derived signal) plus a stricter alias-resolving 403 assert on every point read. Real and multi-layered — but a positive-evidence filter, so it is only as complete as the ingredient catalog it reads.

Docs The feature card

the entity in one handle, one analogy and one constraint box

Authored in cards/allergen.md — the only hand-written source on this page. Everything counted elsewhere is read from the codebase at build time.

“"Never show a recipe that can hurt this user — enforced in the query, not the UI."”

ISthe SC-03 safety guarantee — a user with a declared allergen never sees a violating recipe on any list, explore, pantry-match, or meal-plan screen.
IS NOTa soft "fuera de tu dieta" preference badge (that is the DIET/preferences half, D17) — allergens are a hard exclusion, diets are a soft label.
DECIDESwhether a recipe row is EXCLUDED from a result set (allergens) vs merely FLAGGED (diet preferences).

a bouncer with two lists — a name list (the recipe's self-reported allergen tags) and a face-recognition camera (its ingredients matched against the allergen catalog). You are turned away if EITHER flags you.

AnalogyIn this codebase
name listservices/recipes.py:194
face cameraservices/recipes.py:224
the bouncer only knows faces already in the catalogboot-reconcile keeps the catalog complete

Easy to confuse:

  • the avoid/exclude browse facets (No usar técnica/textura/temperatura) — those are per-search PREFERENCES, not the allergen wall.
  • services/safety.py — that is the SOFT food-safety avisos layer (botulism, salmonella), a different domain from the allergen exclusion.

Where the analogy stops working: the bouncer analogy breaks where the two lists disagree on identity — the SQL join matches the RAW ingredient code, while the point-read assert resolves aliases first, so an aliased ingredient is a "face" only the assert recognizes.

Full card — what & why, for whom, flows, is / is not

What & Why

Gustify's core safety promise (SCOPE SC-03): a user with any tag in DietaryProfile.allergens[] never sees a recipe containing that ingredient — or violating that diet — on any screen, enforced at the database query level so no UI-layer gap can leak a violating recipe. Allergens are a hard exclusion; diet preferences[] are soft-filtered (surface with a "fuera de tu dieta" badge — D17's binary two-list model, superseding D16's three-level proposal).

The wall is positive-evidence: a recipe is dropped only when a signal AFFIRMATIVELY flags an allergen — self-reported restriction_codes (exact JSON-array token, #17) OR an ingredient that maps to the allergen in the catalog (#38/G18 ingredient-derived closure, D67/D69). Excluded on either signal. Because it excludes on evidence rather than defaulting closed, its guarantee is contingent on catalog completeness — the deploy-time boot-reconcile/seed is what keeps restriction_codes fresh and ingredient_restrictions populated (the machinery that closed the earlier fish-allergen leak).

For Whom

  • The family cook and every household co-cook — the person who declared an allergy trusts that no suggestion, list, or plan can surface a dish that violates it. This is the one promise the app cannot break quietly.
  • The apprentice / secondary cook — shares the household allergen constraints; every screen they see is filtered the same way.
  • Whoever prices safety risk — the register on the Risk tab names exactly where the guarantee is contingent (catalog completeness) and where two enforcement mechanisms disagree (alias resolution), so the residual risk is legible, not assumed away.

Flows

  • declare → the user sets allergens in Ajustes / Alergias (cap of 5, MAX_ALLERGENS) or the setup wizard; the heavy danger-toned confirm gate guards REMOVAL (H11), the redo wizard preloads declared allergens so re-onboarding can never silently wipe them to [] (C2), and the R8 allowlist filters any non-canonical code before the write.
  • resolve → load_user_allergens (services/recipes.py:1409) reads the profile per request at query-build; the dialect is resolved from the live bind, so the same builder works on SQLite and Postgres.
  • exclude ★ → every list surface (browse, explore, pantry cookability, meal-plan generation, favorites, saved-modes, planned, cooked, pantry-match) funnels through _apply_recipe_filters (services/recipes.py:654-669), which ANDs both allergen condition sets under if user_allergens: — re-applied on every request, so a once-safe favorite that becomes unsafe is excluded on the next fetch.
  • backstop → the by-id detail, plan, and cook-start point reads call assert_recipe_allergen_safe (services/recipes.py:1226) → 403 before building the body; this assert resolves aliases via the resolution snapshot, making it stricter than the browse SQL join. (assured: C1940 in the journey corpus asserts the 403 while declared and 200 at baseline, live vs staging-e2e — shot-less by design: no UI path reaches a violating detail because the wall already hides the card)
  • heal → deploy-time reconcile_recipe_restrictions re-derives every slugged recipe's restriction_codes and upserts catalog-delta ingredient_restrictions pairs, keeping the positive-evidence wall's inputs complete. (assured: integration corpus C986-C989 proves the reconcile heals drifted codes, and the deploy-verify healthz gate runs it at every push — a browser cannot walk a deploy-time reconcile)

Is

  • An always-on SQL WHERE exclusion on every browse/list/suggest surface — one shared builder, not a per-endpoint reimplementation.
  • Two-signal: self-report tags (exact token, NULL-guarded) UNION ingredient-derived (NOT EXISTS join). Excluded on either.
  • Layered: browse = SQL; point reads (detail/plan/cook) = a stricter alias-resolving 403 assert.
  • Catalog-contingent: a positive-evidence filter kept honest by boot-reconcile/seed completeness.
  • Fed by declaration paths that are themselves guarded (cap=5, R8 allowlist, redo-preserve C2, heavy-confirm-on-removal H11).

Is Not

  • Not a single SQL path. SC-03 is delivered by TWO mechanisms — the browse SQL join and the point-read app-layer 403 assert — that derive their answer along different code paths (verified single_path=false).
  • Not fail-closed. It excludes on positive evidence; a recipe with NULL/omitting restriction_codes AND no catalogued ingredient match is served. The guarantee rests on catalog completeness, not a closed default.
  • Not the diet/preference filter. Diet preferences[] are soft ("fuera de tu dieta" badge); only allergens[] are hard-excluded (D17).
  • Not the avoid/exclude browse facets (técnica/textura/temperatura/equipo) — those are per-search user preferences, not the safety wall.
  • Not the food-safety avisos (services/safety.py) — that is a distinct advisory-warning domain (botulism/salmonella).
  • Not proven by property/fuzz. The SC-03/REQ-07 "randomly-generated profiles × catalog, zero leaks" acceptance signal is documented but unimplemented; coverage is hand-picked fixtures.

Docs Changelog — decisions that shaped it

why the entity behaves the way it does

Source: the entity card's DECIDED section. A decision here is a rule the code obeys, not a plan — the ones with ids are in .kdbp/DECISIONS.md.

DecisionWhat it settles
SC-03 / D-GU1 / R8allergen exclusion is enforced at the SQL query level, never as an application-layer filter for browse — the module docstring and CLAUDE.md bind this.
D17binary two-list model — allergens[] hard-exclude vs preferences[] soft-badge; supersedes D16's three-level severity.
#17exact-token match — allergen codes match as JSON-array ELEMENTS, not substrings (a gluten-free-variant code is not excluded for gluten).
#38 / G18 / D67 / D69ingredient-derived closure — a recipe whose INGREDIENTS break an allergen is excluded even when its self-report omits the code; excluded on either signal.
H6mixing removed (2026-07-08) — the combined-cook allergen guard no longer exists; stored paths are plan + start_session + detail.
MAX_ALLERGENS = 5single source (constants.py + shared/schemas/setup.schema.ts); bound by every write path.
C2 / C3 / H11declaration-path hardening — redo-preserve (never wipe declared allergens to []), cap-is-5-not-3, heavy danger confirm on removal. These protect the wall's INPUT, not the query.
403 not 409allergen conflict on a stored path is FORBIDDEN, distinct from the concurrent-cook 409.

Type colors — one hue per family, deeper = the wider type: int float · Decimal numeric · date · time datetime temporal · str bytes · Text textual · bool · list · dict · Literal structured · UUID identity · None nullable. An uncolored token is a domain alias (an enum defined in this codebase).
Insight icons — the DATA-MODEL lens; the same shape runs over other member kinds later (functions · methods), scoped, never mixed:
  • model — a persisted DB entity: lives in a table, owns FKs.
  • schema — an API / pipeline shape: crosses a boundary, owns no storage.
  • base — derives from NOTHING: no FK out, no field typed by another documented class; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-class flag — field count ≥ 15; the number that makes it a split candidate below.
  • Class N% closest structural twin — % = shared fields over the union (Jaccard); a ≥80% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • orphan — zero API usage AND zero internal references; becomes a deprecation candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoint touches + FK in) · violet = internal (mapped backend files referencing the class). Api-silent is not dead; only a true orphan is.

About this section

The wall lives in services/recipes.py: the two condition builders (allergen_filter_conditions L194, ingredient_allergen_exclusions L224) composed in _apply_recipe_filters L654-669, the per-request resolver load_user_allergens L1409, and the point-read assert assert_recipe_allergen_safe L1226. services/safety.py is the adjacent soft-avisos layer. services/restriction_seed.py + services/reconciliation.py keep the catalog (the wall's evidence base) complete. Declaration surfaces are the settings/setup routes + the web settings safety components. The data model is the dietary profile + the ingredient→restriction catalog.

ContextualWarningRule 89% NEWallergenapps/api/models/catalog.py0 api
1 internal 4
KINDmodel — table ingredient_warnings
DOCSTRINGMaps a canonical ingredient code → an INTRINSIC food-safety advisory it carries (Future-Features SAFE). A SOFT advisory — *how not to mishandle* (e.g. "los porotos crudos contienen fitohemaglutinina; hervir 10 min") — kept DISTINCT from the HARD allergen wall in `IngredientRestriction` (*who can't eat*). Content is PROVENANCE-TAGGED (founder D-PH-1 revised): `source_kind` is `official` (an authoritative citation in `source_ref`, e.g. FDA/MINSAL/WHO) or `ai_default` (no official source found — the advisory is an AI-suggested default and the UI DISCLOSES it as such). `source_ref` stays NOT NULL. `aviso_code` is the stable id surfaced in the derived `recipes.avisos`. System-owned.

ContextualWarningRule
IngredientWarning 89% NEWallergenapps/api/models/catalog.py0 api
1 internal 2
KINDmodel — table contextual_warning_rules
DOCSTRINGMaps (canonical ingredient code + preparation STATE) → a food-safety advisory that applies ONLY in that state (Future-Features SAFE — founder chose the prep/state context). E.g. `huevo` + `crudo` → salmonella caution; `porotos` + `crudo` → toxina danger. Content is PROVENANCE-TAGGED via `source_kind` (`official` | `ai_default`), `source_ref` NOT NULL — same two-tier disclosure as IngredientWarning. Rows ship ahead of the recipe-level trigger: a rule fires into a recipe's `avisos` when that recipe uses the ingredient in `state_tag` (the state signal is wired in a follow-up; the table + content come first). System-owned.

NEWallergenapps/api/services/restriction_seed.py0 api
0 internalno case
KINDfunction · async · 49 lines · layer services
DOCSTRINGReconcile the R8 allergen wall from the in-image catalog on deploy. TWO closures, both fed by the catalog files (mirrors seed_recipe_sensory_on_startup — DEPLOY-ONLY, advisory-locked, NON-FATAL, so a failure logs LOUDLY but never crash-loops boot): 1. BROWSE path — re-derive each slugged recipe's stored ``restriction_codes`` (drifted rows). 2. AI-GENERATION path — UNION the catalog-delta ingredient→restriction pairs into ``ingredient_restrictions`` (insert-only). ``seed_ingredient_restrictions`` seeds only taxonomy ``starter_ingredients``, so delta-only fin-fish (fish-sauce, congrio, …) otherwise never carry fish-free in that table and the AI wall (``reference.resolution .derive_restrictions``) can't derive it. Insert-only ⇒ idempotent, never removes a pair.

KindWhat it is for on this entity
integrationthe wall itself, exercised by deterministic fixtures: self-report SQL exclusion incl. exact-token-no-substring (test_recipes C946-C950, claimed by recipe), ingredient-derived G18 closure + plan/cook rejection (test_stored_allergen C1096-C1105), composition-order allergen-before-novelty (test_novelty C663, claimed by novelty), deploy-time boot-reconcile healing drift (test_restriction_seed C986-C989), dataset drift-guards over every catalog delta (test_allergen_dataset C100-C119), reconcile-requires-a-violates-code (test_reconciliation C982), the meal-plan surface's wall gates — a celiac user's plan never contains a gluten recipe, and archived/now-allergenic planned recipes never leak into the shopping gap (test_meal_plan C592/C599), and the wall's input model round-trip (test_setup_preferences_models C1038). Since P2 (#45) every fixture speaks the CANONICAL allergen vocabulary — the wrong-language codes that silently bypassed the R8 allowlist in test data are gone, so the corpus can no longer pass by matching a wrong string on both sides of the join.
unitthe declaration paths that keep the wall's input honest: recipe-filter dietary sync cap+allowlist+asymmetric-confirm+revert-without-cache-leak (recipeDietarySync C1307-C1320). Additional allergen guards live in settings settingsModel (C1519) and auth setupMapping (C1170-C1178, incl. C2 redo-preserve) — claimed by the settings/auth entities not yet adopted.
journeylive staging-e2e proof: the WALL itself — declaring shellfish-free excludes a violating recipe from browse on the next request of the same session, and a direct point read of its id 403s while declared / 200s at baseline (web-journey-allergen-wall C1939-C1940); plus the declaration paths — cap=5, heavy-confirm-on-removal, cancel-is-no-op, persisted removal (web-journey-settings-allergen C1685-C1687). Captured into the e2e junit corpus since 2026-07-23.
evidencetwo proof sets: allergen-wall (the exclude★ golden path — before/after browse shots, catalog count drop) and settings-allergen (the declaration-path fixes). The backstop flow is deliberately shot-less: no UI path can reach a violating detail BECAUSE the wall hides the card — its proof is C1940's 403/200 assertion pair in the journey corpus, not a screenshot. The heal flow (deploy-time reconcile) is not walkable by a browser; its verification is the integration corpus (test_restriction_seed C986-C989) plus the deploy-verify healthz gate at every push.
coveragenot sliced per entity (repo pytest --cov gate is not path-sliced).
manualthe adoption walk recorded on approval.
deployednothing machine-readable probes the live wall between deploys.

touches GET /recipesPATCH /settings/preferences

What this set shows: Two shots of the same browse catalog in the same login session, before and after declaring a shellfish allergy. In the first, Paila Marina — a shellfish stew — sits in the catalog among 306 recipes, under the banner explaining that results respect your diet and allergies. In the second, taken after the allergen was declared and the page simply reloaded, the catalog counts 280: Paila Marina and every other shellfish recipe are gone from the whole walked pager while everything else renders normally. The companion spec also asserts the backstop off-screen: a direct API read of the excluded recipe's id returns 403 while declared, and 200 again once the declaration is removed — a state no UI path can reach precisely because the wall already hides the card.

claims the legacy pages made that this page refuses to repeat, and why

Claims the legacy cards made that re-verification refuses to repeat:

  • "assert_recipe_allergen_safe guards combined/mix-cook" (h4) — dropped: the combined/mix-cook path was removed by H6 (2026-07-08); current stored paths are plan + start_session + detail only.
  • "the allergen conflict returns 409" (h4) — dropped: all three routes map AllergenConflictError → 403 (api/cooking.py:159, api/recipes.py:912/1073). The 409 in cooking.py is ConcurrentCookCapError; the "409" existed only in the old card's mermaid.
  • "D51/D135 decide the ingredient-derived allergen wall" (h4) — dropped: D51 is a Phase-15 tier decision and D135 is EXPL-BADGE; the real ingredient-derived-allergen decisions are D67/D69.
  • "the avoid/exclude facets are the allergen-safety mechanism" (avoid-exclude) — dropped: those are per-search preference filters (técnica/textura/temperatura/taste/equipo), a separate always-on wall drives allergen safety. Conflating them is the exact error this card refuses.
  • "single SQL path, never an application-layer filter" (framing) — qualified, not repeated verbatim: the BROWSE wall is SQL, but the point-read guarantee is delivered by app-layer 403 asserts, and the wall fails open on absent catalog data.
